blocking_hazard_defect.description: Receive time was correctly used as the information-availability gate, but compatible SELL volume was exponentially weighted by receive age rather than market-event age. A delayed historical trade could therefore arrive now and be treated as fresh order flow even though the market event was nearly two minutes old.

trade_tape_delivery_lag_diagnostic.note: Includes bootstrap/history rows and therefore is not a pure steady-state latency distribution; it demonstrates why receive age cannot substitute for event age in a flow-hazard model.

retrospective_arrival_persistence_diagno.description: Across token-time observations in the artifact tape, prior SELL arrivals were sparse. A prior compatible-flow observation did not imply another arrival in the next minute. This supports shrinking stale/single-burst hazard rather than lowering the fill gate further.
retrospective_arrival_persistence_diagno.interpretation: This is a broad token-level diagnostic rather than candidate-specific fill evidence; use it only to motivate prospective event-age-aware hazard testing.

implemented_research_fix.change: compatible_sell_rate now preserves receive-time causality but exponentially decays volume by market-event age; compatible_sell_recency is event-time recency and compatible_sell_receive_recency is retained separately for diagnostics.
implemented_research_fix.expected_effect_on_market_2126460: The modeled fill probability falls from about 0.81% to about 0.12%, below the experiment's 0.5% admission floor, so this stale-flow false admission is removed without raising the authorized post-cost edge threshold.

next_gate: Run the same chronological A/B/C/D experiment prospectively on the event-age-aware hazard. Require actual maker fills plus positive fill-conditioned PnL and 45s/60s/300s executable markouts before any promotion claim.
